scope: Independent review of the M4 test candidate archive and named native engineering evidence; no holdout or targeted-matrix raw inspected
scope_limits: The candidate is an engineering test archive, not a release. Every named acceptance artifact records release_qualified=false.
The four backend fault probes intentionally pass tools through and record an actual attack effect; they establish outage behavior, not protection during outage.
The recovery probe begins with a timeout, then restores healthy before-tool-call requests and RV decisions without a Gateway restart.
The regression log supports 1049 passed, 18 skipped, one warning and four subtests. Its separate two autonomous regressions are asserted in JSON but not evidenced by this log.
Default 67 rules were packaged but not newly evaluated; experimental 109-rule results do not qualify the default rule set.

The v6 raw runner check records post_uninstall_native_tools_complete=false because it expected runId in execution rows; the saved SDK execution schema supplies toolCallId/sessionKey. The separate offline oracle linked both successful executions to hooks in one run/session, and its acceptance source hash was recomputed. The original v6 check remains false for auditability.

The v6 SDK records read success but does not save the returned text or its hash; write-file SHA is independently checked. This supports completed write and read calls, without a content-equality claim for the read response.
